title: Null Acceptance
description: Distinguishes an optional parameter that may be omitted from a parameter that explicitly accepts null.
question: Does adaptation preserve whether each parameter accepts null?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP tool schemas distinguishing omission from null.
known_issues: A server may reject explicit null even when omission is valid, creating avoidable validation failures.
why: Optional and nullable are different contracts. Conflating them lets a downstream caller express values the source never accepted.

notes.crewai: CrewAI: optional fields are emitted through nullable anyOf wrappers, broadening the accepted values beyond omission alone.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each `inputSchema` as a Pydantic model (`create_model_from_json_schema`), and the model's JSON schema is what `ToolMetadata.to_openai_tool` hands the LLM. Every optional field becomes `Optional[...] = None`, so its schema gains an `anyOf` branch of `null` the server never declared.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `convert_tools_to_openai_schema` emits the strict OpenAI function schema from the Pydantic `args_schema`, which wraps each optional property in `anyOf: [..., {type: null}]`, so the model is offered `null` where the source only allowed omission. `MCPClient._clean_tool_arguments` then drops every `None` argument (and every dict left empty) before `tools/call`, so a null the model sends never reaches the server.

summary: Wrapping an optional field in a union that accepts null changes the source nullability.
